author: Lintuxer
tagline: Needs IceWhale Movies (beta) — play its films on a DLNA TV, the phone is the remote
description:
**Movies-Cast** plays the films of IceWhale **Movies** on a TV in your home
network. Your phone is the remote; nothing is installed on the TV.

- Open the tile (or `http://<your-zimaos>:8097` on the phone), log in with
  your ZimaOS account, pick the TV at the top, then a film
- The TV gets the original file and plays it itself — no transcoding on the box
- Pause, ±30 s, seek bar, stop; "Continue watching" is shared with Movies
- "No sound?" restarts the film with converted sound, remembered per TV
- Name, hide or add TVs by IP; Wake-on-LAN for a TV that is off

**Requirements.** IceWhale Movies (module `zimaos-movies` 0.3.0 or later)
on the same ZimaOS — it is a beta and not in the App Store yet; without
it Movies-Cast has nothing to show. The TV must be a DLNA media renderer:
if it shows up in the TV list on the phone, it is. Tested with an LG
OLED55B9. The LG webOS TV app from the video is not part of this app.

**Android TV** (e.g. Nvidia Shield): Kodi works as a DLNA TV once
"Allow remote control via UPnP" is on (a tester's Shield TV Pro). A
Movies-Cast app for Android TV is a test build, `movies-cast-tv-<version>.apk`
on the release page; in the emulator, AC3 and E-AC3 sound stayed silent.

Guide and source: https://github.com/chicohaager/movies-cast

tips.before_install:
**Needs IceWhale Movies** (module `zimaos-movies` 0.3.0 or later, a beta)
on this ZimaOS. Movies-Cast logs in to it with your ZimaOS account.

**Firewall.** If ZFW runs, it asks about 8097/tcp and 1901/udp — answer
*LAN only*. UDP 1901 carries the TVs' answers to the search.

The program runs on the host network (DLNA discovery) and keeps its
logins and settings in `/DATA/AppData/movies-cast/state`.
